article.headline: No. 1 Nebraska Volleyball Sets Historic 53-Match Regular-Season Winning Streak Record
article.summary: Nebraska volleyball defeated Michigan on Friday night to secure a record-breaking 53rd consecutive regular-season victory.
article.body:
A crowd of 12,707 fans watched at the Crisler Center as Nebraska overcame a first-set loss to storm past Michigan in four sets, finishing 26-28, 25-20, 25-20, 25-14. The win, the 53rd straight for the team in the regular season, officially breaks the previous program record of 52 consecutive victories set during the 2004 and 2005 seasons. This latest result also extends the team's current undefeated streak to 22-0 on the year.

The unbeaten streak remains a critical barometer for the top-ranked Huskers as they defend their standing in the Big Ten. Beyond the record, the match at Michigan marked the second-ever sellout at the venue, matching an attendance high set by the same matchup in 2025. With this momentum, Nebraska maintains its dominance in road and neutral-site matches, now holding a 24-game winning streak that ranks 11th all-time in NCAA history.

According to the official athletics website, the team showcased a balanced offensive effort with five players recording double-digit kills. Virginia Adriano led the charge with a career-high 14 kills, while Harper Murray added 16 kills to the effort. Andi Jackson reached a personal milestone during the match, becoming the 13th Husker in the rally-scoring era to eclipse 1,000 career kills. Setter Bergen Reilly facilitated the high-efficiency attack, which hit .412 overall, by contributing 58 assists and nine digs.

The Huskers have little time to rest following their Friday night performance. The top-ranked squad moves on to face Michigan State on Saturday as they look to protect their unblemished record.

article.headline: Fabio Silva 89th-minute strike snatches draw for Dortmund against Bayern Munich
article.summary: Borussia Dortmund twice rallied to force a 2-2 draw against Bundesliga leaders Bayern Munich.
article.body:
Fabio Silva found the bottom left corner with an 89th-minute strike on the turn, silencing the crowd and denying Bayern Munich a victory in Der Klassiker. The late goal capped a frantic ending to a match that saw the lead change hands twice and both teams frequently testing the woodwork.

For Bayern Munich, the result serves as a precarious defense of their position at the top of the Bundesliga table. While they remain ahead of Borussia Dortmund, the lead is now held only by goal difference. Any slip in performance from the league leaders allows the trailing pack to tighten their grip on the standings, making every point crucial in the mid-season race.

According to the BBC, Bayern Munich initially took the lead through Konrad Laimer, who scored after his own rebound was saved. Harry Kane, fresh off winning the Ballon d'Or, struggled to convert his chances, notably hitting the crossbar with a second-half penalty. Dortmund replied through Serhou Guirassy, who leveled the match with a low effort. Dayot Upamecano restored Bayern’s lead with a close-range header, but the home side could not maintain their advantage as Silva’s late heroics secured the draw. Sky Sports confirmed that despite Bayern’s protests regarding a foul in the build-up to the final equalizer, the goal stood as the visitors clawed their way back.

The draw sees both teams separated only by goal difference at the peak of the German league. Bayern Munich continues to operate under the guidance of assistant manager Aaron Danks as head coach Vincent Kompany recovers following his discharge from the hospital earlier this week.
